section_contracts.title: STANDARD EVALUATION PROCEDURES

schedule_interpretation.instructions: Return schedule_interpretation with assignments, unallocated, and rationale. Each assignment has visit (exact approved label), activity (an exact source phrase), source_path, and source_excerpt (an exact contiguous quotation supporting that relationship). When labels repeat, supply visit_number from visit_records to identify the exact contact. Schedule list strings may be contact labels or prose. For each prose item, return narrative_items with exact source_path, source_index and whole source_excerpt from schedule_items. Only selected strings are removed from the display contact inventory; typed rows and unselected contact labels remain. Selection alone does not preserve its facts: map or retain each selected item's facts as unallocated. If a contact is explicitly stated in narrative but absent from the separate inventory, declare it in visits with visit, optional timing, source_path and source_excerpt; both label and any timing must be exact source phrases. Never turn an activity into a visit. Map every explicitly assigned activity, preserving quantities, conditions and exceptions. Do not infer timing, assign every activity to every visit, or invent a contact. Each unallocated item has source_path and source_excerpt; retain every remaining material fact or genuinely ambiguous relationship there. An empty assignments list is valid only when no explicit relationship is supplied; retain all source text as unallocated then. Existing structured relationships remain authoritative. This is a derived display interpretation, not an edit or new fact in the approved source.

assessment_presentation.instructions: Optionally return assessment_presentation with activity_labels and notes edit lists. Each edit has source_text (exact existing table label or note), display_text, and rationale. Use standalone clinical wording, preserving clinical facts, units, qualifications and visit associations. Remove internal synopsis/source references from display labels and notes. Omit a note with empty display_text only when all its material information is already represented. Keep unique safety, timing and footnote explanations in adjacent prose. Keep genuine numbered forms, instrument names, citations and explained footnotes. Remove a numeral only when source context confirms an orphan footnote marker; uncertainty means retain it. Code does not strip numbers or judge equivalence. =### Context:
We are writing a clinical study protocol document.  
Your task is to generate the **Study Design and Methods** sections.

### Inputs we will provide (with descriptions):
- Study Title: The full official title of the study.
- Study Design: Free text describing the study design as provided in the form.
- Endpoints: The list of primary and secondary endpoints.
- Assessments Schedule: The planned assessments and their schedule.
- Number of Sites: The total number of investigational sites.
- Background: Background and significance text.
- Primary Objective: The main objective text.
- Hypothesis: The hypothesis text.

### What you need to do:
- Generate **studyDesignLong**: an expanded paragraph that integrates studyDesign, numberOfSites, endpoints, and assessmentsSchedule. Mention timepoints only if they are explicitly present in the inputs.
- Generate **methods**: describe bias minimization procedures.
- Generate **masked**: extract masking or blinding details.
- Generate **variables**: present the endpoits gropued.
- Generate **duration**: A very short description of how long will the patients in the study will bethe.
- Determine **studyArm**: Identify if the study is "single arm" or "double arm" based on the Study Design input.

### Important notes:
- Do not invent outcomes, procedures, masking, timepoints, or measurements beyond what is provided.
- Keep the tone professional, neutral, and consistent with clinical protocol style.

### Output format:
Return only valid JSON in the following structure:
{
  "studyDesignLong": "expanded description paragraph",
  "methods": "bias minimization methods",
  "masked": "masking/blinding details",
  "variables": "endpoints in structured text",
  "duration": "duration in a very short text",
  "studyArm": "single arm or double arm"
}

=### Study Title:
A Single-Site, Randomized, Contralateral Eye Trial Comparing Active Sentry at Low IOP vs Ozil at High IOP


### Study Design:
Single site, single-masked, randomized, prospective contralateral eye study.


### Endpoints:
Primary Endpoint: The total aspiration time between groups on the day of surgery.  

Secondary Endpoints:  
- Total fluid volume between groups on the day of surgery.  
- Total phaco time between groups on the day of surgery.  
- Total case time between groups on the day of surgery.  
- Aspiration time during phaco between groups on the day of surgery.  
- Central corneal thickness (CCT) between groups at postoperative day 1 and week 1.  

Exploratory Endpoint:  
- Cumulative dissipated energy between groups on the day of surgery.  


### Assessments Schedule:
- Preoperative: Eligibility evaluation, consent, visual acuity, slit lamp, and CCT measurement.  
- Operative (two visits): Sequential bilateral cataract surgeries with standard surgical findings recorded.  
- Postoperative Day 1: CCT measurement, slit lamp exam, VA testing, AE monitoring.  
- Postoperative Week 1: CCT measurement, slit lamp exam, VA testing, AE monitoring. 


### Timeline
Study Start Date: March 1, 2025  
First Patient In: March 15, 2025  
Last Patient Out: December 15, 2025  
Data Analysis: January 2026  
Final Report Submission: February 28, 2026


### Number of Sites:
One


### Background:
Elevated bottle height (i.e., intraocular pressure, IOP) during cataract surgery impacts corneal tissue and the anterior chamber. Previous studies found Active Sentry at 44–50 mmHg as safe and efficacious as Ozil at 65–70 mmHg, but did not test Active Sentry at lower IOP levels (20 mmHg), which is its main advantage.


### Primary Objective:
To assess the efficiency of the Active Sentry handpiece at low IOP compared with the Ozil handpiece at high IOP.


### Hypothesis:
The Active Sentry handpiece at low IOP is non-inferior to the Ozil at high IOP in terms of surgical efficiency.

  "studyDesignLong": "This study is a single site, single-masked, randomized, prospective, contralateral eye study of the efficiency of the Active Sentry handpiece at low IOP compared with the Ozil at high IOP. Subjects will be assessed pre-operatively, operatively, and at 1 day and 1 week post-operatively. Clinical evaluations will include measurement of visual acuity and central corneal thickness (CCT).

The primary outcome measure will be the total aspiration time between groups on the day of surgery.

Secondary outcome measures are as follows:
• Total fluid volume between groups on the day of surgery.
• Total phaco time between groups on the day of surgery.
• Total case time between groups on the day of surgery.
• Aspiration time during phaco between groups on the day of surgery.
• Central corneal thickness (CCT) between groups at postoperative day 1 and week 1.

Exploratory outcome measures are as follows:
• Cumulative dissipated energy between groups on the day of surgery.",
  "methods": "As a randomized study there is no expected bias. Patient selection will be based on the patient’s interest and the surgeon’s opinion as to whether they are a suitable candidate for sequential bilateral cataract surgery. The data analyzer will be masked.

The measurement of visual acuity will be conducted in a systematic fashion to minimize bias. Individuals conducting visual acuity measures will be instructed to perform the same testing in the same fashion for all subjects, with the same level of encouragement to subjects.

All data collection will be completed through provided Case Report Forms (CRFs) or computer files generated by automated test equipment. All site personnel involved in the study will be trained in regard to conducting study-specific procedures.",
  "masked": "The data analyzer will be masked.",
  "variables": "Primary: The total aspiration time between groups on the day of surgery.

Secondary:
• Total fluid volume between groups on the day of surgery.
• Total phaco time between groups on the day of surgery.
• Total case time between groups on the day of surgery.
• Aspiration time during phaco between groups on the day of surgery.
• Central corneal thickness (CCT) between groups at postoperative day 1 and week 1.

Exploratory:
• Cumulative dissipated energy between groups on the day of surgery.",
  "duration": "Preoperative (≤90 days) to 1 week postoperative",
  "studyArm": "double arm"
}

Pregnant or breastfeeding.  
Participation in another clinical study within the past 30 days.

subjects.inclusion: Preserve the approved inclusion list and its conditions. A separately stored screening interval supplies a criterion only when the approved eligibility lists do not already express it. If it is already an exclusion, keep it there once rather than adding its inverse to inclusion. Preserve scope, exceptions and timing.
subjects.exclusion: State the disqualifying conditions, preserving the approved source meaning and scope. A negative eligibility requirement must not become a reason to exclude someone who meets it. If the approved source itself is ambiguously classified, retain it for manual inspection rather than silently reversing the rule after approval; resolve future classification during source intake.
study-design.design: Keep the complete approved endpoint inventory, but state a shared endpoint time point once for the group. Use one primary-endpoint statement and a compact secondary-endpoint list instead of repeating 'Secondary endpoint' and the same timing in every item. Retain genuinely different timings and qualifications.

Keep the primary statement, secondary group and exploratory group distinct. The response format renders paragraphs before lists: when secondary outcomes use lists, put the exploratory outcome in its own final list group labeled 'Exploratory endpoint:' instead of inserting an exploratory paragraph between the secondary introduction and its items. Preserve genuinely different timings.
evaluation-procedures: The source-derived table owns the visit/activity inventory. Read the section's assessment_presentation labels and notes alongside the approved schedule. Return assessment_presentation.notes edits for redundant notes: source_text must exactly match a supplied note; display_text is empty only when every material fact is already represented. Otherwise retain unique timing anchors, conditions, safety instructions, measurement details and footnote explanations. Give a factual rationale for each edit. Keep the body to a short table introduction; do not repeat the endpoint or assessment list beneath it.
endpoint-criteria.study-completion: Summarize the supplied final study assessment/completion date and administrative closeout separately in at most a short paragraph. Reference the visit schedule and record-retention sections for their details. Planned completion is distinct from early study termination; place early-stopping grounds only in the source-supported termination section.
icf.procedures: State the visit count and phases once, then explain each visit once. Use the supplied visit names and actual timing/window labels in those visit entries, with plain-language explanations beside them. Avoid a second visit inventory or repeated timing list after the details.

Keep operative care separate from research-specific activities when the source makes that distinction. Do not turn unspecified follow-up, order of procedures, monitoring, or exit rules into new obligations.

Use the same supplied visit labels and explicit visit numbers as the Protocol. When a source schedule groups repeated occurrences (for example one operative visit per eye), use its phase names rather than inventing expanded Visit 1/2/3/4 numbers. Explain the occurrence count separately when supplied. Preserve the actual timing in each visit entry using plain language; no separate timing recap is needed.

For ambispective studies, distinguish existing historical records from future participant visits. State each future contact mode and its actual assessments; historical abstraction is a staff task unless the source explicitly calls for a participant visit. Explain study-result return policies without adding an unmasking promise to an unmasked study.

Include a supplied missed-contact or rescheduling policy once alongside the relevant visit details, preserving its attempt limit and existing window. The drafted prose owns that rule; no second formal source sentence is needed.
icf.duration: Give expected enrollment once using the approved count and unit, then describe how long a participant takes part and the final follow-up anchor. Leave the visit-by-visit itinerary and procedure details in PROCEDURES.

Keep sponsor enrollment and data-analysis periods out of the participant duration paragraph unless needed to resolve an explicit source ambiguity. Never imply those study-wide phases extend the participant's follow-up, and do not add extra safety visits absent from the source.
icf.privacy: Keep consent withdrawal instructions usable for every supplied site. In a shared multi-site consent, refer participants to their enrolling site contact in the contact section rather than calling the first site everyone's site. Preserve authorization expiry, access roles, retention, genetic-data and results policies exactly as supplied.
icf.injury: Write directly to the participant using the supplied injury contact, evaluation arrangements, payer and compensation limits.
